verdict: Northrop Grumman grew sales 7% to $11.1B, won $16B of new awards to lift backlog to a record $110B, and raised its 2026 guidance — demand is outrunning even its own plan.

kpis.label: Backlog
kpis.note: Record — $16B of net awards, a 1.5x book-to-bill ratio

segments.name: Product sales
segments.note: Weapons, aircraft, spacecraft and electronics delivered to customers. By business: Aeronautics Systems sales were $3,575M (+14%), Mission Systems $3,155M (+2%) and Space Systems $2,749M (+2%), before intersegment eliminations.

segments.name: Service revenues
segments.note: Support, maintenance, training and logistics services. Defense Systems sales were $2,307M (+12%) before intersegment eliminations; total company sales of $11,122M are after $664M of sales between Northrop's own segments were eliminated.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — executives, finance, legal and other overhead not tied to a specific contract, up 10% YoY.

otherDetail: Other income of $29M, net: a $167M non-operating pension benefit and $20M of other income, partly offset by $158M of interest expense on the company's debt.

takeaways.title: Aircraft lead the growth
takeaways.text: Aeronautics Systems sales rose 14% to $3.6B and Defense Systems 12% to $2.3B. All four businesses grew, and total sales rose 7% to $11,122M.

takeaways.title: Backlog hits a record
takeaways.text: Northrop won $16B of net new awards in the quarter — 1.5 dollars of new orders for every dollar of sales — taking the backlog of contracted future work to a record $110B.

takeaways.title: Guidance raised
takeaways.text: The company raised its 2026 outlook: segment operating income guidance rose $65M at the midpoint and mark-to-market-adjusted EPS guidance rose $0.70 at the midpoint. The tax rate was just 13.4%, which also flattered net earnings.

footerNote: Sales are split the way Northrop's income statement splits them (product vs service); business-segment sales in the notes are before $664M of intersegment eliminations. Cost of revenue = product costs of $7,198M plus service costs of $1,572M.
